run.executedVia: Playwright runner, no browser: ServiceNow read over cnit and the Scripted REST API as sf.integration, Salesforce read over the sf CLI and anonymous Apex against the deployed classes. Every case reads both sides.

case.title: No Apex test coverage exists

steps.text: List the Apex classes in the org.
Look for any test class belonging to this org rather than to an installed package.

records.label: Unmanaged classes carrying @isTest
records.query: Tooling API, NamespacePrefix = null, SymbolTable modifiers contain isTest

observations: The org ships four `devedapp` classes of its own, two of them named *Test. They are packaged, cover nothing in this project, and do not count toward the org-wide figure the same way — filtering on the name alone would report test coverage that does not exist. Note also that CafAttestationService contains the substring "test", so a name-based filter claims the class under test is its own test.

Fine for a Developer Edition org, blocking for any move toward production: Salesforce requires 75% org-wide coverage to deploy. This belongs in the test summary as a release risk, not in the defect list. HANDOFF open item 5.
expected: Coverage on CafSyncHealth, CafEvidenceService and CafAttestationService is zero.
Reported as a release gate, not a defect: Salesforce requires 75% to deploy to production.
actual: 9 Apex class(es) in the org: CafAttestationService, CafDashboardController, CafEvidenceService, CafSyncHealth, CafTaskService (plus 4 packaged: devedapp.DeveloperEditionUtils, devedapp.DeveloperEditionUtilsTest, devedapp.PostInstallScript, devedapp.PostInstallScriptTest).
CafSyncHealth: 0 covered / 167 uncovered; CafAttestationService: 0 covered / 50 uncovered; CafEvidenceService: 0 covered / 132 uncovered
case.verdictReason: Zero test classes and zero coverage on all three service classes — confirmed as a release gate.
